question:
The initial velocity of a purified enzyme was measured at 8 substrate concentrations, without inhibitor and with an inhibitor at 10 µM. Measurement error is Gaussian with SD 0.974 µM/min.
Data:
| substrate (µM) | inhibitor (µM) | initial velocity (µM/min) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0 | 3.12 |
| 2.1 | 0 | 4.11 |
| 4.5 | 0 | 6.3 |
| 9.7 | 0 | 13.6 |
| 20.6 | 0 | 24.5 |
| 44 | 0 | 28.2 |
| 93.8 | 0 | 38.2 |
| 200 | 0 | 40.3 |
| 1 | 10 | 1.41 |
| 2.1 | 10 | 1.7 |
| 4.5 | 10 | 4.44 |
| 9.7 | 10 | 9.38 |
| 20.6 | 10 | 15.2 |
| 44 | 10 | 22.7 |
| 93.8 | 10 | 30.7 |
| 200 | 10 | 37.7 |
Candidate models (parameters unknown, all positive):
- Noncompetitive inhibition: v = Vmax·S/((Km + S)·(1 + I/Ki))
- Uncompetitive inhibition: v = Vmax·S/(Km + S·(1 + I/Ki))
- Competitive inhibition: v = Vmax·S/(Km·(1 + I/Ki) + S)
Which candidate model most likely generated these data? Rank the candidates, and give the features of the data that decide it, the key evidence, and one further measurement that would best confirm the top pick.
